app.Response.description: The Response struct is used for wrapping the API response with a code, message, and data.

code.description:
Code is the HTTP status code or a custom code used to indicate the result of the request
@example 200

data.description:
Data is the response data (can be any object or null)
@example {"id": 1, "name": "John Doe"}

msg.description:
Msg is the message that describes the result of the request
@example "Request successful"

battle_royale_teams.description:
BattleRoyaleTeams is filled for battle-royale titles (PUBG Mobile), which list every
team's placement and points instead of two sides.

info.description: Crawlora is a hosted web-data and SERP API: call documented REST endpoints and get normalized JSON instead of HTML to parse — across search/SERP, maps and local, e-commerce, app stores, social, media and finance. One API key; Crawlora runs the proxy rotation, headless browsers and parsing behind the scenes. Billed pay-on-success: charged only on a successful 2xx response, 1-10 credits per call, with a free tier of 2,000 credits per month and no card. A hosted MCP server (mcp.crawlora.net/mcp) exposes the same catalog as agent tools. Search endpoints accept `q` as a universal alias for whichever search-term parameter they document (`query`, `term`, `keyword`, or Amazon's `k`), so one parameter name works across the whole catalog; an explicitly supplied documented name always wins.
info.title: Crawlora API

get.description: Returns one GosuGamers news or features article by numeric id: type, title, teaser, section, publish and update times, headline image with caption, authors, the full text as plain text and related articles. An unknown id returns not found. Take `id` from gosugamers-articles.

parameters.description: Numeric article id from gosugamers-articles
parameters.name: id

get.description: Pages the GosuGamers news and features archive (51,051 articles), newest first, with optional `section` and `type` filters: id, type, title, teaser, section, publish time, author, image and URL. `section` is one of the 15 sections that carry articles (the six esports titles, Wild Rift, Free Fire, Battlegrounds Mobile India and the editorial sections entertainment, genshin-impact, honkai-star-rail, zenless-zone-zero, honor-of-kings and umamusume-pretty-derby); an article can belong to several sections. `type` is `news` or `features`. Paged with `page` and `page_size` (up to 100). Use gosugamers-article with a returned id for the text.

parameters.description: Article section; one of dota2, counterstrike, lol, valorant, mobile-legends, pubg-mobile, wild-rift, free-fire, battlegrounds-mobile-india, entertainment, genshin-impact, honkai-star-rail, zenless-zone-zero, honor-of-kings, umamusume-pretty-derby; omit for all
parameters.name: section

parameters.description: Article type; one of news, features; omit for both
parameters.name: type

parameters.description: 1-based page; defaults to 1
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 100; defaults to 10
parameters.name: page_size

get.description: Returns the other recorded meetings between two GosuGamers teams as seen from one match: tournament, start time, both teams with ids, tags and final scores, winner flags and the match URL. The given `match_id` itself is left out; `game` is required by the upstream but does not narrow the list. Take the ids from gosugamers-matches, gosugamers-results or gosugamers-rankings. Two teams with no other meeting return an empty list.

parameters.description: Game section of the match; one of dota2, counterstrike, lol, valorant, mobile-legends, pubg-mobile, wild-rift, free-fire, battlegrounds-mobile-india
parameters.name: game

parameters.description: Numeric id of the match whose other meetings are wanted; that match is left out
parameters.name: match_id

parameters.description: Numeric id of the first team
parameters.name: team1_id

parameters.description: Numeric id of the second team
parameters.name: team2_id

get.description: Returns the game sections whose match pages this API reads: `dota2`, `counterstrike`, `lol`, `valorant`, `mobile-legends`, `pubg-mobile`, `wild-rift`, `free-fire` and `battlegrounds-mobile-india`, with display names. Use a slug as `game` in the other gosugamers endpoints.

Returns one GosuGamers match: start time, tournament, stage, round, best-of, finished flag, both opponents with score, placement, world ranking and country, the number of games in the series and linked streams with language and viewer count. All of `game`, `tournament_id` and `match_id` are required; an id that does not belong to the stated tournament returns not found. Battle-royale titles can list more than two opponents. The `games` list gives each game's id for gosugamers-match-game.

parameters.description: Game section; one of dota2, counterstrike, lol, valorant, mobile-legends, pubg-mobile, wild-rift, free-fire, battlegrounds-mobile-india
parameters.name: game

parameters.description: Numeric tournament id from gosugamers-matches or gosugamers-results (tournament.id)
parameters.name: tournament_id

parameters.description: Numeric match id from gosugamers-matches or gosugamers-results (id)
parameters.name: match_id

get.description: Returns one game of a GosuGamers match: the map, each team's score, side and first-pick flag, the picks or bans with the player (agents, heroes or champions where the title publishes them), the lineups, round or half scores (Counter-Strike and Valorant), every team's placement, kills and points for battle-royale games (PUBG Mobile) and VODs. Take `game_id` from the `games` list of gosugamers-match. Fields a title does not publish are empty. An unknown game id returns not found.

parameters.description: Numeric game id from the games list of gosugamers-match
parameters.name: game_id

get.summary: GosuGamers single game (map) of a match

get.description: Returns the next upcoming and currently live esports matches from GosuGamers, for one `game` or across all games, 10 per page by default and up to 100 with `page` and `page_size`: start time, tournament, stage, round, both teams and the match URL. `total_rows` reports how many matches the site lists. Use gosugamers-match with the returned tournament and match ids.

parameters.description: Game section; one of dota2, counterstrike, lol, valorant, mobile-legends, pubg-mobile, wild-rift, free-fire, battlegrounds-mobile-india; omit for all games
parameters.name: game

parameters.description: 1-based page; page 1 with the default size is read from the public page, any other page or size from the site's JSON API; defaults to 1
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 100; defaults to 10
parameters.name: page_size

get.summary: GosuGamers upcoming and live esports matches

get.description: Returns one GosuGamers player: in-game name, real name, country, GosuGamers Elo rating and world and regional ranking, win/loss/draw record and win rate, streak, career earnings in USD, social links, the current team and previous teams with join and leave dates. A player of a different game than `game` returns not found.

parameters.description: Game section; one of dota2, counterstrike, lol, valorant, mobile-legends, pubg-mobile, wild-rift, free-fire, battlegrounds-mobile-india
parameters.name: game

parameters.description: Numeric player id from gosugamers-team (roster[].id)
parameters.name: player_id

get.description: Returns the GosuGamers Elo team ranking for one `game`, globally or for one ranking region (`region_id`, taken from the `regions` list in the response; 0 is Global), with an optional team name prefix `q`: rank, team id, name, tag, Elo, previous rank and rank change. Paged with `page` and `page_size` (up to 100); `total_rows` reports the size of the ranking. A `region_id` that the game does not list returns an invalid-parameter error.

parameters.description: Game section; one of dota2, counterstrike, lol, valorant, mobile-legends, pubg-mobile, wild-rift, free-fire, battlegrounds-mobile-india
parameters.name: game

parameters.description: Ranking region id from the regions list of the response; 0 is Global; defaults to 0
parameters.name: region_id

parameters.description: Team name prefix, up to 100 characters
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: 1-based page; defaults to 1
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 100; defaults to 10
parameters.name: page_size

get.description: Returns the most recent completed esports matches from GosuGamers, for one `game` or across all games, 10 per page by default and up to 100 with `page` and `page_size`, with final scores and winner flags. `total_rows` reports how many results the site lists. Use gosugamers-match with the returned ids for opponents, ranking and streams.

parameters.description: Game section; one of dota2, counterstrike, lol, valorant, mobile-legends, pubg-mobile, wild-rift, free-fire, battlegrounds-mobile-india; omit for all games
parameters.name: game

parameters.description: 1-based page; page 1 with the default size is read from the public page, any other page or size from the site's JSON API; defaults to 1
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 100; defaults to 10
parameters.name: page_size

get.description: Returns the groups (child tournaments) of one stage of a GosuGamers tournament, each with its format (for example Knockout), result type (for example Bracket), status, start time and the teams in it with ranking and country. Take `tournament_id` from gosugamers-tournaments or gosugamers-matches and `stage_id` from the stages list of gosugamers-tournament. An unknown stage, or a stage of another tournament, returns an empty list.

parameters.description: Numeric tournament id from gosugamers-tournaments or gosugamers-matches
parameters.name: tournament_id

parameters.description: Numeric stage id (stages[].id) from gosugamers-tournament
parameters.name: stage_id

get.description: Returns one GosuGamers team: name, tag, country, logo, GosuGamers Elo rating and world and regional ranking, win/loss/draw record and win rate, current streak, career earnings in USD, social links, the roster with join dates and the team's next upcoming matches. A team of a different game than `game` returns not found.

parameters.description: Game section; one of dota2, counterstrike, lol, valorant, mobile-legends, pubg-mobile, wild-rift, free-fire, battlegrounds-mobile-india
parameters.name: game

parameters.description: Numeric team id from gosugamers-matches, gosugamers-results or gosugamers-match (teams[].id)
parameters.name: team_id

get.description: Returns the completed matches of one GosuGamers team, newest first, across the games it plays: start time, tournament, both teams with ids and final scores, winner flags and the match URL. Paged with `page` and `page_size` (up to 100, default 10); `total_rows` is the team's full history. An unknown team id returns an empty list. Take `team_id` from gosugamers-rankings, gosugamers-results or gosugamers-team.

parameters.description: Numeric team id from gosugamers-rankings, gosugamers-results or gosugamers-team
parameters.name: team_id

parameters.description: 1-based page; defaults to 1
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 100; defaults to 10
parameters.name: page_size

get.description: Returns one GosuGamers tournament: name, status, start time, description, LAN flag, venue and country, prize pool in USD when listed, sponsors, stages with their status and the next upcoming matches. A tournament that belongs to a different game than `game` returns not found.

parameters.description: Game section; one of dota2, counterstrike, lol, valorant, mobile-legends, pubg-mobile, wild-rift, free-fire, battlegrounds-mobile-india
parameters.name: game

parameters.description: Numeric tournament id from gosugamers-matches or gosugamers-results (tournament.id)
parameters.name: tournament_id

get.description: Returns the teams entered in one GosuGamers tournament: id, name, slug, logo, GosuGamers ranking, country and team URL. Both `game` and `tournament_id` are required; the upstream does not narrow the list by game, and an unknown tournament id returns an empty list. Take the tournament id from gosugamers-tournaments, gosugamers-matches or gosugamers-results and use a team id with gosugamers-team or gosugamers-team-results.

parameters.description: Game section of the tournament; one of dota2, counterstrike, lol, valorant, mobile-legends, pubg-mobile, wild-rift, free-fire, battlegrounds-mobile-india
parameters.name: game

parameters.description: Numeric tournament id from gosugamers-tournaments, gosugamers-matches or gosugamers-results
parameters.name: tournament_id

get.description: Returns the casters, hosts and analysts assigned to one GosuGamers tournament: id, name, game, roles, broadcast language code, country, image and profile URL. An unknown tournament id, or a tournament with no listed crew, returns an empty list. Take the tournament id from gosugamers-tournaments, gosugamers-matches or gosugamers-results.

parameters.description: Numeric tournament id from gosugamers-tournaments, gosugamers-matches or gosugamers-results
parameters.name: tournament_id

get.description: Lists GosuGamers esports tournaments, optionally for one `game` and one `state` (`all`, `ongoing`, `upcoming`, `past`), with an optional name prefix `q`: id, name, game, status, start time, prize pool with currency and USD value, participant count, featured flag and the tournament URL. Paged with `page` and `page_size` (up to 100); `total_rows` reports the size of the filtered list. Use gosugamers-tournament with a returned id and game for stages and upcoming matches.
